#1941. Ashley Young names Premier League star Manchester United should sign to replace Bruno Fernandes

Ashley Young reckons it is time for Manchester United to move on from Bruno Fernandes and feels there is a Premier League star who should be signed to replace him.

Fernandes has consistently been the Red Devils’ best player since joining from Sporting in January 2020.

However, at 32 years old and with new manager Mauricio Pochettino arriving this week, doubts over whether Fernandes will remain the focal point of the team are being raised.

The United captain is into the final few months of his contract and has reportedly rejected two offers of a new deal.

The club has the option to extend his current contract by another month, which would prevent Fernandes leaving on a free transfer in the summer, but he could still be sold in 2027 if that option is taken up.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Former Red Devils man Young reckons it is time to move on from Fernandes and thinks the man to replace him is Nottingham Forest and England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

The former Wolves star turns 27 in January and Young feels now is the time for Manchester United to make him their main man, replacing Fernandes.

‘He’s been unbelievable for the club, the standout performer,’ Young said of Fernandes on Overlap Daily. ‘But there’s been so much that’s come about. He’s turned down another contract, we’re hearing.

‘You want to build around a player. He’s 33 next year. Age is nothing but a number, but he’s not in his peak. I wouldn’t say past it, but he’s getting older now.

‘For me, I would go and sign Morgan Gibbs-White. I’m just throwing that name out there. But you’re thinking a number 10 and you want to build a team around a player.

‘He’s young, he’s hungry, he’s just got in the England squad. I think he’s got the capabilities to go and play for – no disrespect to Nottingham Forest – a bigger club. And I think he’s someone that Manchester United need, in his peak years.

‘I think he’s shown more than enough at Nottingham Forest to be able to go and say I can play for a bigger club like Manchester United and take the weight of that.’

As much as signing new players will be on the agenda for the new Manchester United manager, getting rid of unwanted squad members may be the bigger test.

Gary Neville feels there needs to be a significant cull over the next few transfer windows, with some big names ideally being axed at the end of the season.

‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, [Matthijs] De Ligt would go, [Noussair] Mazraoui would go, [Mason] Mount would go, first wave next summer. [Marcus] Rashford if you can, and [Joshua] Zirkzee,’ the former full-back said on Stick to United.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at [Luke] Shaw, [Harry] Maguire, [Diogo] Dalot, Bruno [Fernandes], that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on [Carlos] Baleba and [Andrey] Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’

#1940. Who makes up Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff at Manchester United?

Manchester United have turned to Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager, and a new backroom staff will be joining him for his return to the Premier League.

After identifying ex-Tottenham boss Pochettino as the desired replacement for sacked head coach Michael Carrick, Man Utd quickly agreed personal terms - before approaching the USA to extract their target from a four-year contract only signed following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

It has been reported that the total compensation package United will have to pay the US Soccer Federation could be north of £10million, once fees for Pochettino’s staff have been included.

Assistant manager Jesus Perez has worked with Pochettino since his first job in management, employed initially as an analyst at Espanyol in LaLiga.

After building a strong relationship with Pochettino, Spaniard Perez was promoted to No2 when the Argentine was appointed manager of Southampton in 2013, and has been his assistant at every job since.

Perez and Pochettino joked about the United job during the World Cup, with the former apparently very keen on working at Old Trafford.

There are four other members of staff likely to make the move across the Atlantic.

Miguel D’Agostino is a former team-mate of Pochettino’s, with the duo having played together at Newell’s Old Boys in their native Argentina.

Initially working as a scout for Pochettino at Espanyol, D’Agostino has also followed his compatriot from club to club since then.

Toni Jimenez is another to have worked with Pochettino at every club he has managed so far, plus the US national team. A goalkeeping coach, Jimenez first linked up with Pochettino in 2011 at Espanyol.

The penultimate member of coaching staff mentioned in reports has not been involved in Pochettino’s setup as long as the others, but has a very close relationship to the former Chelsea manager.

Sebastiano Pochettino is Mauricio’s son and started working within his father’s coaching team at Spurs. He has continued in his role as a sports scientist.

Silvia Tuya - full name Silvia Tuya Vinas - is a strength and conditioning coach, currently employed by the USMNT.

Tuya will become the first female coach of the men’s first team squad at Old Trafford, creating history ahead of a new chapter for Manchester United.

The strength and conditioning coach will be familiar with creating such history, having previously become the first female coach in the history of the USMNT’s senior squad when she joined the backroom staff in October 2024.

#1939. ‘One of my favourite loans’ - Carl Ikeme recalls Middlesbrough FC experience as Championship prediction made

Carl Ikeme has fondly recalled his loan spell at Middlesbrough - and believes anything but automatic promotion this season would be disappointing for the club.

The retired goalkeeper spent the entirety of his career on the books of Wolverhampton Wanderers, who loaned him out on nine separate occasions.

He spent time at Middlesbrough during the 2011/12 season and made 10 appearances during the reign of Tony Mowbray.

A number of the 40-year-old’s former clubs are in the Championship promotion race, therefore it is something he is keeping a close eye on.

“I think there’s some strong teams,” he told The Yorkshire Post. “I think out of the teams that were left in the Championship, they (Middlesbrough) were the standout team.

“They nearly did it last year as well, they've probably learnt from that experience. They've got a great set-up at Boro as well, a really good club. It was one of my favourite loans, if not my favourite loan, great club, great set-up.

“They've got a great owner as well and he's been there for a long time and he really takes his time and knows what he's doing. I'm not saying they're the team to beat but they've hit form quite soon. I think that obviously Wolves and West Ham will be there or thereabouts as well.

“I think they'll be disappointed if they don't go up automatically this year but that being said, with Wolves, West Ham and Burnley coming down, it's going to be tough to get up for anyone. You've got the teams in and around the play-off picture, you've got the chasing pack as well.”

Middlesbrough came within a whisker of promotion last term, losing to Hull City in the play-off final at Wembley.

Kim Hellberg’s side did not spend too long licking their wounds and sit second in the table after 15 games.

“Out of the teams that were left in the Championship, they do look like the strongest,” Ikeme said. “I think Wolves will be hoping to kick on as the year goes on but Boro do look like one of the teams that will be in and around it.”

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Harvey Barnes has warned Bruno Guimaraes that his return to St James’ Park with Arsenal is exactly what Newcastle need to spark themselves into form.

#1936. Leeds United midfielder Sean Longstaff lifts lid on ‘tough year’ and makes Newcastle United comparison

Leeds United midfielder Sean Longstaff has conceded his move to Elland Road has not gone completely to plan.

The 29-year-old signed for the Whites as part of their post-promotion recruitment drive in the summer of 2025, making a £12m move from his boyhood club Newcastle United.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He started his maiden campaign as a midfield regular but missed the weeks in which Leeds turned their season around through injury.

Opportunities were limited upon his return and competition in the middle of the park has only intensified in his second season.

He told The Official Leeds United Podcast: “I’d be lying if I said it’s been the easiest year I’ve ever had. It’s been a tough year.

“There’s probably been times, at home, especially, there’s times where you’re not that nice to be around. Ultimately, I made the decision to come to Leeds. I took my family away from the comforts of being at their home. I’ve took a newborn baby away from his grandparents to bring him down here for me to enhance my career.

“Obviously, at the minute, it’s not gone probably to the perfect plan. But I don’t think life ever does.”

Longstaff was handed his first league start of the season before the international break, completing 90 minutes in Leeds’ 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur.

He made his 200th Premier League appearance in the game and the reaching of the milestone in such a valuable win served as a reward for his perseverance.

The midfielder said: “For me, I take training as serious as possible. Whether that’s the day after a game, whether it’s during the week, you’ve got to train as if you’re going to play.

“And then ultimately, if you don’t play, that’s not in my control. I can’t control it. All I can control is, make sure I’m fit enough to play when I get a chance, make sure I’m sharp enough, make sure my mentality is right.

“If I get a chance, I want to try and show what I can do, whether that’s for 30 seconds whether that’s a for, come on at half-time, or whatever the case may be. I can’t control other people’s decisions. All I can control is the controllables.”

Longstaff may not have seen the level of action he wanted in West Yorkshire, but has spoken of the club with great affection.

He has compared the Whites to Newcastle, who he made 214 appearances for before departing.

He said: “It’s still close to home so it didn’t feel like you were moving away miles. It’s not until you probably get down here, everyone says Leeds is a massive club, but until you get here, you don’t realise how big it is.

“I came with an expectation of ‘it’s going to be Newcastle’s this and Leeds is that’. Then you get in, you think ‘oh actually, Leeds is so similar.

“Apart from the kit, everything else felt exactly the same. Obviously the only difference is me being from Newcastle and not from Leeds, but actually got to know a lot of people from the city and they were telling us stuff. The way they speak about Leeds is the way I felt about Newcastle. The more you meet people, the more you realise it’s massive.”

#1935. Premier League panel confirm ruling on Kai Havertz incident in Hull City’s defeat to Arsenal

Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty in their 1-0 win over Hull City before the international break, a Premier League panel have ruled.

Martin Odegaard struck the decisive goal for the Gunners, who played host to the Tigers on November 7.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hull were widely lauded for their defensive grit in the game, although the division’s key match incidents panel has claimed they should have been penalised.

Tigers defender Nobel Mendy held on to Gunners forward Kai Havertz yet even after a VAR review, a spot-kick was not awarded.

The panel said: “Although Harvertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz.

“Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded.

“The panel consdered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.”

Arsenal will not feel too aggrieved given they secured three points, but it would most likely have been a different story had they not.

Reflecting on the game, Tigers defender John Egan told the club’s media team: “I feel like we put a really good performance in, put a lot into the game. You know, what we worked on all week, we put on the pitch. Maybe [it was] a little bit of a missed opportunity the way we played.

“I think we deserved a result. We made it hard for them. [I’m] proud of the lads. I really thought we played really well, so mixed feelings. Disappointed not to get a result, but also a really tough place to come. We played really well.

“When you play a game like this, you know, you do everything you can to get a result. We did that. You know, on another day the ball falls to us. Today, it fell to them.

#1934. Exclusive: Charlton boss Nathan Jones among managers objecting to FA rule change

Charlton manager Nathan Jones is among a number of head coaches in English football’s top four divisions to have objected to the reduction in how many yellow cards leads to a touchline ban.

Standard Sport understands that at a recent managers’ meeting, Jones and other head coaches from clubs among the 92 argued a 2023 change in FA rules towards stricter punishments for technical-area misconduct remains unjustified at a time when football managers have never faced greater pressure and volatility.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is incongruous with an increasingly demanding working environment.

Head coaches across the Premier League and EFL are understood to have this season been shown research that suggests managers’ behaviour usually improves once they reach three bookings.

Managers are regularly reminded of a variety of regulations including technical-area misconduct rules during meetings with the FA’s disciplinary teams, who often present research and statistics to contextualise changes to rules or emerging trends.

Ahead of the 2018-19 season, new rules were introduced to clean up touchline behaviour. Managers across the FA Cup, EFL, Carabao Cup, EFL Trophy and National League could receive yellow and red cards for the first time, with four yellows resulting in a one-match touchline ban.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is unreasonable

Premier League managers would receive only verbal cautions for “irresponsible behaviour” but then the top flight fell in line with the same level of punishment from 2019-20 onwards.

A further update was made ahead of the 2023-24 campaign when the FA launched a new ‘Participant Behaviour Charter’ as part of its ‘Love Football, Protect the Game’ campaign, developed alongside the Premier League, EFL, Women's Super League, Women's Championship, National League System (Steps 1–4), and PGMOL (now Pro Ref), with input from the League Managers Association (LMA) and Professional Footballers' Association (PFA).

The charter’s aim was to improve the image of the game and maintain a positive environment. Four yellows for a managerial suspension was reduced to three and has remained so ever since.

A new cut-off for technical-area cautions was introduced this season. Managers who receive their third technical-area booking after the 37th round of EFL league matches do not incur an immediate suspension. At that point an automatic one-match touchline ban is triggered only if a fourth yellow card is picked up in a subsequent game.

Compared with its peak, the number of technical-area cautions issued has decreased by 17 per cent since the introduction of the ‘Participation Behaviour Charter’, FA sources say.

Under the FA’s ‘Laws of the Game’, other staff and substitutes in a technical area can also be cautioned or even sent off.

In certain circumstances, managers and head coaches can get booked or sent off on behalf of the misconduct of others in their technical area if the fourth official reports a situation deserving of punishment to the referee but cannot verify who in the technical area committed the offence. In such situations, FA rules state cards can be shown to the “manager or most senior coach in [the technical] area”.

#1933. Belgian journalist admits Sylla may be ‘more inclined’ to move to England: “His dream destination”

AC Milan have been heavily interested in Massire Sylla recently, but it seems they may struggle to sign him, let alone in January.

It’s no secret that Milan want to sign a central defender and whilst Goncalo Inacio is the leading name, he’s not the only one in the mix. Instead, there are several public names of interest and Sylla is one of them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

First linked by Matteo Moretto, his name has become more popular in reports linking the Rossoneri to defenders and he seems like a concrete target for the January mercato. Yet, it seems like it will be difficult to bring him to San Siro.

Speaking to MilanNews, Het Nieuwsblad journalist Tjorven Messiaen looked at Massire Sylla and what his future had in store.

In Italy, there’s been talk of AC Milan’s interest in Sylla. What’s being said about him in Belgium?

“I saw that AC Milan have linked him with him. In Belgium, we discovered him through social media, and the USG hasn’t confirmed anything yet. It’s possible, however, that AC Milan has drawn attention to the boy, because he’s playing great football.

“His move to AC Milan is unlikely to materialise in January, however, as both Sylla and the club would be more inclined to listen to offers from the Premier League. He’s the kind of player who would be a perfect fit for the English league.”

What are his main strengths and best qualities?

“He’s young, he’s good in duels, he’s quick. He’s also very good at ball control. He’s a complete defender; he has the potential to become one of the best, and he’d be a perfect fit in the Premier League, which, among other things, is Sylla’s dream destination.”

What aspects of his game still need improvement?

“It’s hard to say, especially since his growth in recent months has been impressive. I’d say he needs to gain more experience, which will come simply by playing. So I don’t see many things he needs to improve to take the next step in his career.”

Do you think Union Saint-Gilloise (USG) would be willing to let him leave in January, or do you think any transfer discussions will be postponed until the summer?

“I don’t think USG will let him leave in January. The only possible scenario, which I don’t think will happen, but which is the only solution anyway, is for USG to sign him in January but keep him at least until the end of the season, especially since the club never sells its best players in January.

“I also think interested clubs could spend a lot of money, but Union won’t let him leave in January.”

Could you describe him in three adjectives?

“Quick, physical, and full of character, because he’s someone who always has problems when he has to make decisions.”

“Considering his development, I’d say Pacho. He came from nowhere in Belgium, developed, moved to Frankfurt, and then ended up at PSG. In Sylla’s case, I think he’ll go straight to the Premier League. He has everything it takes to be perfect for this league.”

He’s still very young. Do you think he’s ready to play for a big club in a big city like Milan?

“He’s still very young, but he’s humble, calm, and we mustn’t forget that he arrived last year, in January, from the Norwegian second division. He played very little last year, but he’s very strong mentally and has started this season as if he’s been playing with this team for years.

“I can’t imagine USG without Sylla today, especially since we’re talking about one of the best defenders in the league. At the end of the season, he’ll make a significant leap in his career, but in my opinion it won’t be AC ​​Milan because he’s waiting for the Premier League. And from what I know, several English clubs are already ready to make him a player.

“So AC Milan could give him a try, but it will require a big project and a lot of money.”

We shall have to see how January develops and whether he could be sold on the project. However, it certainly doesn’t bode well from these comments.

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:28 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:04 EST, 12 November 2026

It's a story which extols the virtues of loyalty and leadership in the proper sense.

More than anything, though, Andy Robertson’s achievements in football are – and always will be – reminders of what’s possible when a talented individual takes rejection as their motivation to redefine themselves in the eyes of the world.

Even though it’s been told many times before, the tale of the full-back’s determination to bounce back from being shown the door as a teenager by Celtic will never grow old.

Without having the character to overcome such adversity, he would not have been caught in the safety net at Queen’s Park. There would have been no moves to Dundee United and Hull. No Champions League and title-winning medals from his time with Liverpool. No first cap for his country.

In terms of a life lesson for those aspiring footballers who may find themselves in a cul-de-sac in their own careers, it has few equals.

All being well, Robertson will make his 102nd appearance for Scotland against North Macedonia, equalling the record tally of his idol and great friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Andy Robertson will go level with Kenny Dalglish as Scotland's record cap holder on Friday

Both men are proud Glaswegians and Scots who bonded throughout their time together at Anfield. Dalglish would be the first to admit, though, that their respective paths have been distinct.

With a God-given talent so bright it could blind you, Dalglish was a superstar in the making before he wore a Scotland jersey for the first time against Belgium in 1971.

Coming in a friendly in Poland in 2014, Robertson’s first appearance only arrived after those early struggles.

It took huge character for him to even get that far. To add a century more across a dozen years under four different managers is a gargantuan achievement.

Football has a funny habit of throwing up strange co-incidences. Yesterday happened to be 40 years to the day since Dalglish won the last of his caps in a 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

Characteristically, before he took his own walk down memory lane, the man who’ll join him on that mark this evening was at pains to give the Anfield icon his rightful place.

‘It’s not really about me,’ Robertson insisted. ‘For how long the record stood, for starters, for what he (Dalglish) achieved in his career, for the person he is... tomorrow is another reason for our country to honour one of the greatest players that has played a game. He’s definitely the greatest in Scotland.

Dalglish scored 30 goals in his 102 caps and is regarded as Scotland's greatest ever player

‘Obviously, in terms of the number, I will stand side by side with him. But I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been to our country.

‘Because, for me, he was arguably the best player in the world at one time and will always be the greatest in this country, no matter what happens in the future.

‘He’ll always be the first one to do X, Y and Z. I just think that shouldn’t be forgotten.

‘Tomorrow is definitely a reason to do that for Kenny.’

There is, though, still no understating what Robertson has achieved across 12 years. Playing for Scotland wasn’t always the joy that it’s been in more recent times.

‘We get looked after so well off the pitch,’ he offered. ‘That probably wasn’t always the case when I first came in.

‘Under Gordon (Strachan) in my first qualifying campaign, I think I was still young enough to not think too much about it. But then I also remember under Alex McLeish and then the start of Steve Clarke, there was a real disconnect between the country and the players.

‘There wasn’t too much love for the players. We were getting 10,000, 15,000 inside Hampden. That was the most difficult time, especially as captain and being at Liverpool as well.’

He stuck at it and never shirked responsibility. In time he was able to chalk up the numbers because the side steadily improved and broke through the glass ceiling.

Robertson shares a laugh with Nathan Patterson ahead of the visit of North Macedonia

‘Of course, I would be sitting here with a few less caps if we hadn’t been successful,’ he reflected. ‘The fact that we got to two Euros, a World Cup and all the warm-up games and things like that resulted in me having an extra maybe 15 caps.

‘What makes it more special to me is the fact that we’ve managed to achieve things.’

All of this was beyond his wildest dreams at the beginning. A late substitute for Barry Bannan in a friendly in Warsaw on March 5, 2014, he can still hear Gordon Strachan whispering in his ear.

‘He basically said, “Don’t be scared, don’t go into your shell”,’ he recalled. ‘He said, “The reason I’ve picked you is because you’re brave. I see you bombing up and down the pitch for Dundee United”. He said, “Go and be that player”.

‘I always remember the first ball came to me and the words were ringing in my ears. I think I carried it 30 yards forward. It gave me the confidence to just go and try and play exactly the way I was playing under Jackie McNamara.’

Four years later, by then a Liverpool player, Robertson was handed the armband by McLeish following Scott Brown’s retirement.

‘That made me grow up and made me realise what it took to become a leader,’ he reflected. ‘I kind of grew into it. I believe that I became the captain that I wanted to be.’

It was only when he equalled McLeish’s 77 appearances that the prospect of one day equalling or surpassing Dalglish entered his head.

‘I think everyone in the room and everyone who personally knows me well enough knows that personal achievements aren’t really what I focus on,’ he said. ‘But I would lie if I said this wasn’t one that I’ve chased.

Like Dalglish, Robertson is a Liverpool icon having made 378 appearances for the Anfield club

‘I think when I overtook Darren Fletcher (80 caps), when I was in the 80s, it felt like ages for me to get to Jim Leighton (91). Then I thought I’ve only got one more person to go.

‘That’s when I started thinking about it a little bit more, starting to believe that it might happen, started to wind Kenny up a bit more that it was going to happen.

‘I think that was maybe when I realised that this was maybe possible if I got lucky with injuries, if I kept playing for Liverpool.

‘Sat here today, if it happens, it’s something I couldn’t be more proud of. My international career has been everything for me.’

To wear the armband at one international tournament would have been a laudable achievement in itself. To do so three times would have seemed an impossible feat in those difficult early days.

The hunger to repeat the trick at Euro 2028 is as strong as ever.

‘I’ve always kept pushing,’ he said. ‘We’re always trying something new. My wife asked me a similar question last week when we were talking about it. I was going to try and catch Gemma Fay (203 caps), but I think that might be a little bit too far from me...’

#1930. Premier League panel confirm ruling on Jayden Bogle incident in Leeds United’s win over Tottenham Hotspur

The decision not to send Jayden Bogle off in Leeds United’s win over Tottenham Hotspur has been supported by a Premier League panel.

Leeds defeated Spurs 1-0 at Elland Road on November 7 and the losing side felt the hosts should have been reduced to 10 men.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Marauding wing-back Bogle caught the back of the ankle of winger Mathys Tel, which forced the wideman out of action.

VAR (video assistant referee) did not call referee John Brooks over for another look and Bogle was not carded for the challenge at all.

The incident sparked plenty of controversy but Brooks’ call has been backed by the Premier League’s key match incidents panel.

The panel said: “This was a split decision with the majority supporting the referee's on field call of no red card. The panel considered this to be a clear foul but the majority felt Bogle was looking to challenge with his right leg and his left leg came down on the back of Tel's ankle without the speed, force or intensity to be serious foul play.

“They felt that the contact made was very clearly reckless, but below the threshold for a red card. Two panellists felt that the challenge was sufficiently dangerous to merit a red card.

“The non-VAR intervention was also supported, 3:2, on the basis that the majority considered the challenge to be reckless, therefore not a clear and obvious error.”

Spurs signalled their intention to appeal the decision and former Premier League referee Graham Barber felt Bogle should have been sent for an early bath.

He said: “I thought it was a very, very poor challenge, it was reckless at best but you could describe it as dangerous and endangering the safety of the opponent, and did it endanger the safety of the opponent? Well, the answer is probably yes, because he had to leave the field of play about five minutes later.”

#1928. ‘Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty’ in Hull win as Premier League panel confirm incorrect offside

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel has voted unanimously that Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty against Hull.

The Gunners beat Hull 1-0 in the final match before the international break to go five points clear at the top of the Premier League.

However, it could have been a much more comfortable afternoon had Arsenal been given a penalty in the first half, when it was still goalless.

Kai Havertz went down in the box as he made a run in behind, having been pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

It was not initially seen by the officials but VAR advised the referee to stop play and consult the pitchside monitor.

Farai Hallam deemed that while Havertz had been fouled, he was in an offside position and therefore a free-kick was given to Hull.

The KMI panel have now confirmed that was the incorrect decision due to the foul taking place before Havertz became active.

All five members of the group voted that both the on-field decision and the outcome of the VAR intervention was wrong.

“Although Havertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz,” the panel explained.

“Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded. The panel considered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.”

The panel added: “Being in an offside position, in itself, is not an offence.

“IFAB Law 11 says that a player in an offside position at the moment the ball is played or touched by a team-mate is only penalised on becoming involved in active play.

“If a player is fouled before becoming involved in active play, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence. Therefore, in this instance, Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty.”

#1927. Moises Caicedo reveals why he asked to come off for Ecuador in latest Chelsea scare

Moises Caicedo has revealed he asked to be substituted at half-time playing for Ecuador as Chelsea were handed a scare during the international break.

Ecuador played friendly matches against Costa Rica and Bolivia, picking up 2-0 victories in both games.

Caicedo played 84 minutes in Quito in what was Marcelo Gallardo’s first game in charge on Saturday, named in the starting XI again on Tuesday.

The former Brighton star was replaced halfway through that game, later revealing he was ‘not feeling well’ with Chelsea’s game against Leeds United on Saturday in his thoughts.

‘No, I didn’t feel very well, so I asked to come off instead, because I know I have another commitment with my club.,’ Caicedo told reporters. ‘So, I’ll try to get there as soon as possible and recover.’

Caicedo missed Chelsea’s opening game of the season against Fulham, suffering a calf injury 14 minutes after coming off the bench in the following game against Brighton.

He was ruled out of the next three games but has started Chelsea’s last five in the Premier League.

He was also a doubt heading into the game against Sunderland before the international break.

During the international break, the 25-year-old opened up on his recent fitness issues.

#1925. Mauricio Pochettino’s first six Manchester United games confirmed as brutal opener awaits

Manchester United are now preparing for life with Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.

Pochettino is believed to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford as he replaces Michael Carrick, who was sacked last Thursday with the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

The appointment of Pochettino has been driven by the Argentine's high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

His consistency of performing at the highest level of football across multiple leagues is an additional factor.

This will be Pochettino’s fourth spell in the Premier League, having previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea to varying levels of success.

As the latest new era at Old Trafford officially gets underway this next week, here is a everything to look forward to once Pochettino gets settled in...

As communicated in the official club statement, Pochettino’s start date is November 18 - after USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final second leg against Haiti.

He is expected to take charge of Man Utd training for the first time ahead of the showdown against Liverpool three days later.

United won both meetings with Liverpool last season, including a rare victory at Anfield, but Pochettino has not tasted victory at that ground since his Southampton days in the 2013-14 campaign.

As Man United travel to Lisbon, Portugal to face Sporting in their next Champions League assignment, it means it’s successive away games at the start of Pochettino’s tenure.

That means Brentford’s trip to Old Trafford on November 28 will serve as Pochettino’s first home game in charge.

We have already mentioned the first three, but it will be an interesting start for Pochettino as Newcastle (a) and Coventry (h) follow on from there in the Premier League.

The run concludes with a Champions League showdown against RB Leipzig on matchday six of this season’s league phase, where United will hope to put themselves in a strong position to qualify for the last-16.

It’s a mixed bag, Pochettino’s Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) spells offer cause for optimism.

That said, the Argentine oversaw four wins and a draw from his first six Spurs and PSG matches, before going one better with five wins from his first six matches in charge of the USMNT.

#1923. ‘Wasted’ – Paul Ince questions £50m Man Utd transfer decision

Paul Ince still cannot wrap his head around Manchester United’s decision to spend £50million on Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window.

Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.

Santos enjoyed an encouraging pre-season, but started only four of United’s first ten Premier League matches under Michael Carrick before his sacking.

Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival may represent a fresh start for the £50m midfielder, but Ince believes United would have been better served spending that money elsewhere over the summer.

‘Why did they spend £50m on Santos?’ Ince told The Sun. ‘That’s £50m wasted. They could have put that into the defence or bought a striker.

#1921. Mauricio Pochettino has been told which FIVE Manchester United deals to complete before end of the season

Gary Neville has called on Mauricio Pochettino to complete an overhaul at Mancheter United, naming five players to be moved on by the end of the season.

The former Man United defender has also suggested another four or five players for the chopping block in a ‘second wave’ of exits.

Having previously commented that the Red Devils’ current defence would lead to relegation, it is no surprise that Neville focused on shipping out defenders.

But Neville fears that a complete reset of the Man Utd squad could take three seasons for Pochettino to complete.

Analysing the squad, Neville said on The Overlap’s Stick to United podcast: “Out of the defenders he’ll keep [Luke] Shaw because he knows him and he’ll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries and you’ll have to manage him.

“He’ll keep [Harry] Maguire because he’ll trust him and think he’s basically a soldier, someone who can do a job for him.

“He’ll keep [Leny] Yoro because he’ll think there’s something to work with. [Ayden] Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in.

“I’d keep Bruno [Fernandes], I’d keep Kobbie [Mainoo], I’d keep [Youri] Tielemans, [Mason] Mount would have to go.

“[Andrey] Santos - Mauricio may like him because he’s young, quite mobile, he’s aggressive, he might get something out of him. Him and [Carlos] Baleba will be in that middle bit. Mount’s the one that goes definitely, in that midfield section.”

Neville then went on to explain that Marcus Rashford’s wages meant he needed to be moved on at the ‘earliest opportunity’.

#1920. Eli Junior Kroupi stance on Arsenal transfer revealed as Bournemouth make decision for January window

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is targeting a move outside of the Premier League despite interest from Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham, according to reports.

Kroupi joined Bournemouth in a £12 million deal from French side Lorient last year and scored 13 goals in his first season in the Premier League.

The 20-year-old has suffered a disrupted start to the new campaign as he required surgery on a foot injury sustained during a pre-season training session in Austria in July.

Kroupi returned in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win away to Manchester United on October 25 and has made three more appearances as a substitute for Marco Rose’s side.

During the international break, Kroupi was handed his senior debut for France as he featured in the 3-1 defeat to Italy, as well as in the 2-1 win over Turkey.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The French striker has attracted interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham, while Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona have also been monitoring his progress in the Premier League.

However, David Ornstein has claimed that Kroupi will look to move overseas when he leaves Bournemouth, although the club are not looking to sell the forward in the January transfer window.

‘There was a big story recently about Alex Scott possibly leaving in the January transfer window, that was conditional on Bournemouth receiving £100 million and being in a really strong position in the Premier League where that becomes a bit of a no-brainer because in six months’ time he’ll have a year to go on his contract and it’s a very different conversation,’ Ornstein said on The Athletic FC’s podcast.

‘Kroupi has got much longer on his contract for a start, so there’s no massive need to sell in a way you would consider selling Scott.

‘He’s been out injured for longer as well, so I think Bournemouth want to make use of him this season and they don’t think their chances of recouping significant value in the summer will be much worse than in January, probably better actually.

‘My information around Kroupi is he would like to move at some point, outside of England.

‘You’ve seen very heavy reporting around PSG and Barcelona. If he continues to show the level of form that he was displaying prior to his injury, the biggest clubs in world football want him.

Mauricio Pochettino officially starts work as Manchester United manager today, and could make Calvin Bassey his first signing. Liverpool are also monitoring young talent, with Mexican midfielder Gilberto Mora among their targets. The Reds are now leading the race for Lamine Camara, who came close to joining Chelsea on deadline day during the summer transfer window. Follow all the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Chelsea’s former techincal director Michael Emenalo has taken up an advisory role at Leicester City.

The Athletic reports that the Nigerian, who was with the Blues for five and a half years, is part of a team of consultants that is helping the Foxes with their future planning.

Manchester United are set to back Mauricio Pochettino the January transfer window.

Sky Sports reports that the Red Devils are prepared to sanction some signings for their new manager in the winter, with the club currently sat in the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino, who arrived at Carrington to begin work on Wednesday, will be tasked with guiding United away from the bottom three and as high up the top-flight table as he can, while also seeing how far he can get his new side in the Champions League.

Mauricio Pochettino has listed the three things he is hoping to bring to Manchester United in his first message to fans.

The Argentine arrived at his new club on Wednesday, touching down in Manchester immediately after overseeing his final game in charge of the United States.

In his first message to United fans, posted to the club’s social media channels, he said: “I am looking forward to meeting you guys.

“I have heard so many good things about you. I hope we bring all the happiness, working together and connect[ion], so that it is going to be a special season, and to make our players fight on the field and get the results we deserve.”

Manchester United have confirmed the departures of five members of staff after Mauricio Pochettino began work as the club’s new manager on Wednesday.

The Argentine was pictured arriving at Carrington for his first day in charge of the Red Devils, having flown immediately over after his final match with the United States.

Gary Neville has called on Mauricio Pochettino to complete an overhaul at Mancheter United, naming five players to be moved on by the end of the season.

The former Man United defender has also suggested another four or five players for the chopping block in a ‘second wave’ of exits.

Having previously commented that the Red Devils’ current defence would lead to relegation, it is no surprise that Neville focused on shipping out defenders.

But Neville fears that a complete reset of the Man Utd squad could take three seasons for Pochettino to complete.

Teddy Sheringham has delivered his reaction to JJ Gabriel announcing his Manchester United exit.

Speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds, Sheringham said: "I think it's absolutely absurd.

“I don't know all the ins and outs but I wish JJ Gabriel well because he looks like a lovely little footballer but blimey, there are troubles ahead for him at this rate without a doubt if these are the demands when he’s still only 15."

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has been urged to reject any advances from Chelsea, and sign for a “bigger” club.

Chelsea’s pursuit of Scott was well documented in the summer, with the Blues seeing two bids rejected by their Premier League rivals, even though the England international had turned down an offer of a new contract.

As such, the 23-year-old, who is out of contract at Vitality Stadium in the summer of 2028, could be allowed to depart in the January transfer window for around £100million.

Standard Sport have previously reported that Bournemouth are open to selling their prized midfielder in the new year if Premier League survival is looking likely and Marco Rose’s side are currently seventh in the table following four straight wins.

Manchester United transfer target Yasin Ayari appeared to pour cold water on any potential move to Old Trafford - before implying that he is keeping his options open.

Ayari has been a key part of Brighton’s bright start to the Premier League campaign, hitting three goals in nine appearances.

Ayari is out of contract this summer leading to speculation regarding his future. United are said to be among the clubs keeping an eye on his situation.

They are far from the only club credited with an interest in the 23-year-old, though. Premier League leaders Arsenal, Serie A outfit Roma, and Turkish duo Fenerbahce and Galatasaray are all reported to be keeping tabs on the Swede.

But, speaking from the Swedish national team camp this week, Ayari appeared to play down reports linking him with a move away from the AmEx: “I’m at Brighton and I’m happy where I am. Things are going well for me right now. Then we’ll see what’s to come.”

JJ Gabriel has confirmed his decision to leave Manchester United in a statement, with Real Madrid expected to win the race to sign the highly-rated young winger.

The 16-year-old has played in United’s academy since 2020 and was expected to start appearing in the first team this season.

Until, that is, he made the shock decision to lodge a transfer request in September, amid reports he and his entourage were frustrated with his lack of first-team opportunities.

United worked hard to convince him to stay and offered him a new contract, but the player has not trained at the club for some time and is now expected to join Real Madrid. He will leave Old Trafford without having made a senior appearance.

After months of speculation as to where he might end up, Gabriel has now issued the clearest update yet on his situation, confirming his decision to leave United in a post to his Instagram page.

Speaking over clips of himself playing for the club, he said: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

“Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I’ll always treasure.

“To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”

#1918. Mauricio Pochettino to sign two-and-a-half year deal to replace Michael Carrick at Man United - as it emerges he WILL take charge of USA game in early hours of Wednesday, just days before crunch Liverpool clash

Published: 10:58 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:28 EST, 12 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will face a brutal start to life at Manchester United with the prospective Red Devils boss set to manage the United States days before his debut at Liverpool.

United have moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer, and he is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Daily Mail Sport understands Pochettino will take charge of both of the United States matches during the international window.

The US take on Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final first leg on Saturday, with the second fixture then taking place in Cincinnati on Tuesday evening, but would likely finish at around 2am GMT.

Pochettino would then have to travel to Manchester following the match to link up with the Red Devils' squad for the first time, likely on Thursday.

The Argentine would then have limited time with his players before a daunting trip to Anfield to face rivals Liverpool on Sunday in a blockbuster first match in charge.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the United States upcoming matches against Haiti

Pochettino will coach in the early hours on Wednesday morning in Cincinnati before travelling to Manchester

The Argentine would have limited time to prepare his side for Sunday's match at Anfield

Man United are said to be relaxed over Pochettino taking charge of his final two matches as US boss before starting as their new head coach.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10million.

The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.

Pochettino is set to take over a Man United side languishing in the Premier League relegation zone following just one win in their opening ten matches.

The trip to Anfield would be the first of a run of eight matches in 29 days, as Man United juggle Premier League and Champions League football.

Pochettino is set to succeed Michael Carrick, whose departure as the Red Devils' boss was officially announced on Wednesday morning.

Pochettino will face a tight turnaround to prepare his new side for the daunting clash on Merseyside

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

In a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Carrick's backroom team have also left the club with Pochettino set to bring his own staff to United.

Assistant boss Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson have all gone, although United didn't initially confirm the news because not all of them were at the training ground this morning and had to be told in person.

#1916. Cardinale says MSE will give Milan ‘financial muscle’ and reiterates: “I will never sell”

Gerry Cardinale has commented on the launch of AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE), stating that he will never sell the club.

Yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had launched the new holding company to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’. From the new stadium to the NBA Europa project, there are big plans for the company.

Brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Big 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position. It doesn’t mean that we will see less of Cardinale though, quite the opposite.

In an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Cardinale outlined exactly what he wants to achieve with MSE and explained why he will never sell the club. Silvio Berlusconi 2.0, as he calls it, with the goal of taking Milan back to the very top.

Cardinale, what benefits will AC Milan gain from the holding company?

“The driving force behind deals like this is to provide AC Milan with the financial muscle needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.

“I will transform the club’s financial profile with the resources that will come from the stadium, the San Donato Arena, and the other activities we are working on with NBA Europe.

“I’m doing everything I can to ensure that, when we want a player, no one can tell me, ‘You can’t sign him because you can’t afford him.’ Currently, only Premier League clubs are able to invest such sums and secure top players.

“If I want to bring AC Milan back to the top of European competition, not just in Italy, we need to figure out how to compete with the world’s top clubs.”

This project confirms that your commitment to Milan is long-term…

“Yes. I will never sell AC Milan. Never. And this is a project to get them back to winning ways. I’m not willing to tolerate it taking a long time to achieve this. I want to do it as soon as possible. We’ll see how quickly…

“My goal is to consistently win Scudetti and, of course, return to the Champions League. Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the foundation to make all this possible.”

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

Could your “recipe” also be valid for Serie A?

“Of course, even for Serie A. In my opinion, it wouldn’t have been a good deal to sell 30% of the league’s international TV rights when JP Morgan made that offer. That’s not how Serie A can return to the top of Europe.

“It needs to be done through business planning and by creating every opportunity to generate new revenue. Like we will do with Milan Sports & Entertainment.

“We will be the first to build a stadium since 2011, and that’s a huge achievement. I started working on it when I bought AC Milan, and finally… the right time has arrived.”

Do you think others will follow you on this path?

“No. Some may do it, others may not. We know what it takes to innovate and change. To avoid continuing to practice Einstein’s definition of insanity, according to which everyone wants a different outcome, but doesn’t want to do anything different to get it.”

How long do you think it will take to complete the other projects that will be part of the new holding company?

“I think the NBA is negotiating with the Euroleague, but one way or another, if they can’t reach an agreement, NBA Europe will still launch. Perhaps the first batch of new franchises for Europe will be announced at the end of the year or in early 2027.

“We will see when that happens… We own the land in San Donato, and if I’m granted the Milan franchise, I will be able to start construction fairly quickly because we already have planning permission for a 20,000-seat arena.

“We will also continue to explore opportunities and hold discussions within the tennis world and to organise a tournament in Milan. Finally, we are already making progress in building and launching a hospitality and facility management company.”

Does your plan include organising and managing hospitality services for other clubs’ stadiums as well, not just the new San Siro?

“Yes, the model is the company I created in 2009, called Legends Hospitality. I created it with the New York Yankees and the Dallas Cowboys. Now that company is worth several billion dollars.

“We not only sell premium seats, suites, merchandise, and hospitality, food, and beverage services for Yankee Stadium and Cowboys Stadium, but also for other clubs. I would like to adopt the same model here, probably in partnership with another club.”

Not many football clubs in the world have established an organisation like the one you are leading…

“Exactly. My ambition is to compete with the best clubs in the world. I want to do so thanks to my global vision of the world of sports and entertainment.

“There aren’t many multi-sports platforms in the world that also own some of their own facilities, and we want to add AC Milan to that list. To compete with them and then be better.”

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”

The English Premiere League makes about FOUR TIMES as much money in TV broadcast rights as Serie A does – €4.6 billion per season (£3.84 billion – £1.68 billion domestic, £2.17 billion international).

Serie A’s TV broadcast rights give it €1.144 billion per season (€894 million domestic, €250 million international)

Total stadium revenue among all the clubs in the English Premier League is also about 2.3 x higher than total stadium revenue for all the clubs in Serie A – over £1billion per season in the EPL (€1.3 billion) compared with €435.4 million per season in Serie A.

It was not always this way. In the 1980s, English football was beset with old, rotting, unsafe stadiums, hooliganism, and low TV revenues.

In 1992, the First Division clubs broke away from the rest of the English Football League (EFL) to form the Premiere League, and began negotiating TV contracts on their own, as well as embarking on a program of enlarging and upgrading their football stadiums. The richest teams began building completely new, large modern stadiums with premium suites, etc.

Meanwhile, nothing much has changed in Italy – most of the stadiums remain municipal owned and small and old.

Ticket prices in the EPL are also generally on average about twice as expensive as in Italy.

So yeah, Serie A had its glory days in the 1990s, as wealthy magnates like Berlusconi infused their personal wealth into their clubs. I remember Fox carried Serie A football on TV in the United States back then. If you wanted to watch the English Premiere League, it was a bit of a struggle to find the matches on TV in the U.S back in the 1990s.

All that changed as the Premiere League steadily built up its international marketing and negotiated ever improved TV contracts. It began to require clubs that were promoted up to the EPL to upgrade their stadiums to meet a certain minimum seating capacity.

And so, today, when Italians complain about how Italy and Serie A can no longer compete with the English Premiere League for the best players, how the EPL hugely overpays for all its star players, the reason is that the EPL makes a $HIT TON MORE MONEY than Serie A does, across the board, in TV income (the biggest factor for the entire league), and stadium income.

That’s why Gerry wanted a new and better stadium, and why he has often talked about Serie A needing to do better marketing and improve its TV contracts.

You can’t get the best players in the world if you can’t compete financially with the richest and most watched football league in the world, which happens to be the English Premiere League right now.

Here in the US, EPL matches are carried by NBC Sports by subscription (about $130-$200 a year). NBC pays the Premiere League $450 million per season to carry English football on TV in the USA.

Serie A matches are carried by Paramount/CBS in the USA (a $90 per year subscription – it went up from $60 after the Ellison Oligarchy mergers). CBS had been paying Serie A $75.8 million per year for those TV rights. However, Serie A with its great marketing and negotiating expertise was unable to improve or renew that contract and so Serie A is currently just going year to year with CBS and getting less than $30 million a year.

Do you see the difference now in the major sources of income between the Premiere League and Serie A??

So yeah, absolutely, Gerry is right to complain about needing to get Serie A some better negotiators and marketers to improve on its TV contracts.

#1915. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

While the Three Lions were beaten on that occasion, it would be a favourable draw given they have won two of the last three meetings against the Dutch - including the Euro 2024 semi-final.

The simulator hasn't been as kind to France as they've been paired with Spain, a team they have lost to three times in a row since victory in the 2021 final.

In addition, the simulator has thrown up two other eye-catching fixtures with Norway taking on Germany, and Portugal continuing the defence of their crown against Belgium over two legs.

#1914. Pochettino says ‘give me time’ as he prepares for Man Utd venture

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino defiantly stated, "You will see, give me time", before jetting off to begin his role as Manchester United head coach.

The Argentine rounded out his duties with the United States by beating Haiti 2-0 in the second leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory.

Following that fixture in Cincinnati, Pochettino flew straight to Manchester, then headed to the Red Devils' Carrington training complex.

United find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone after a tumultuous 2025-26 campaign thus far.

Club legend Michael Carrick was sacked after winning just one of 10 top-flight fixtures this season.

Former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea coach Pochettino was hired in his place, but wanted to see out the Haiti double-header.

Following the game, he was told by former USA and Manchester City midfielder DaMarcus Beasley that, "Manchester is blue, it always be blue".

Pochettino replied to the quip by saying: "You will see. Give me time.

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 13, 2026

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time, it's adrenaline you want to feel. We need to add our common sense.

"We know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.

"The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us every day, we are a much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

United later posted a video on social media of Pochettino arriving, in which he said: "I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege, to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work."

He's here. Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino! https://t.co/MOhRCv79hq

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

Pochettino's first assignment could scarcely be a more difficult one, with United travelling to Anfield to face fierce north-west rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

He will be the first United boss to see his maiden league game in charge come against Liverpool.

This is the latest into a league season (MD11) that Liverpool and United have faced with one of the sides in the relegation zone since November 1972, when bottom side Man Utd beat league-leaders Liverpool 2-0 at Old Trafford.

#1913. Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners, relegation race, Golden Boot and more

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The 2026-27 Premier League season is just days away from resumption following the final international break of the year, and with it the return of some familiar faces.

Mauricio Pochettino is back in English football after a spell in international management, he has succeeded Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach. Meanwhile, Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace.

After 10 games of the campaign, both Man United and Palace are in the relegation zone. So will these appointment help to drag them out of the bottom three?

At the other end of the table, Arsenal have made a solid start to the defence of their Premier League crown, and appear to have a surprise challenger as confusion has set in around Manchester City.

Plenty of questions to be answered over the next six months, and the Standard Sport football reporters, Matt Verri, Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau, have had a go at predicting what is in store for the remainder of the season.

MV: Arsenal continue to look ruthlessly efficient and should be confident of defending their title. The defensive unit is absurdly good, the midfield depth is ridiculous, and it means the forwards only need to deliver a moment or two per match.

Even whey they are not at their best, Arsenal are just so difficult to beat. That is the case over 90 minutes and it should be the case over 38 matches again.

DS: No reason to change what I predicted at the beginning of the season, which was for Arsenal to win the Premier League title. If anything, the opening 10 rounds of games have made me more convinced the Gunners won’t be caught and will defend last season’s crown.

Arsenal fans may continue to worry about a lack of goals from their forwards, but their defence is on track to perform even better than last season’s, and that gives other challengers a daunting task to catch them. Arsenal could genuinely win the title by as many as 15 points.

ST: Arsenal were favourites to retain the Premier League title before the season started and that has not changed 10 games in.

Pochettino told FIVE Man Utd deals to complete before season ends

Manchester City started the season with a perfect record, but their performances have begun to suffer, perhaps impacted by the looming threat of a potential points deduction.

Brighton will surely fall away, while the likes of Liverpool and Chelsea are capable but lacking consistency.

MV: Now it gets harder. Liverpool have not quite put it all together yet but there are signs that they will. I’ll go for them to just edge second ahead of Brighton, who have been superb this season but could fade slightly if they go deep in Europe as expected.

Chelsea have the firepower in attack to secure fourth and Unai Emery can work his magic to get Aston Villa into fifth.

DS: My top five, in order, back in August was Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea, then Liverpool. That needs some revising.

Man City are difficult to predict because of the unknowns involved in their impending punishment for financial rule breaches, but they may just about hold on to second (pre-punishment). In third, there are signs Liverpool could come good, particularly if Alexander Isak can stay fit.

Brighton will drop from second but stay strong enough to finish in the Champions League in fourth. Chelsea in fifth — though their performances must improve.

ST: I think the teams who currently occupy the top five spots will all remain there, it is more a case of which position each team will finish. Arsenal will be champions, while I believe Brighton will slip to fifth when the going gets tough in the spring.

Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea are all interchangeable. But I think it will end up being City second, Liverpool third and Chelsea fourth.

MV: Assuming a resolution is reached this season, it is hard to see how Manchester City can avoid a sanction that leads to relegation. I predicted in the summer that Sunderland would go down and that has been reinforced over the first ten games. That squad looks stretched and sorely lacking in goals.

Thomas Frank was abysmal at Tottenham but can do enough to solidify things at Crystal Palace. Instead, Coventry will not quite have enough to stay up.

DS: Along with many others at the time, I predicted the three promoted teams to go straight back down. Even though Hull made a good start, Ipswich have been decent and Coventry seem to have turned a corner, I still expect those three to be weaker than Sunderland, Fulham, Crystal Palace and other strugglers as the many months progress. Coventry, Hull and Ipswich still.

ST: With so much time left in the season, it really is anyone’s guess who will get relegated. Just two points separate the Premier League’s bottom club Crystal Palace and 17th place Coventry, so if Thomas Frank gets it right, the Eagles can quickly pull away from danger.

I think Fulham, Nottingham Forest and Coventry are all capable of getting dragged into the relegation zone.

Sunderland, Forest and Coventry will be the three to go down.

MV: Thierno Barry gets enough chances in front of goal to challenge, while Alexander Isak is starting to show why Liverpool were so determined to sign him. However, it is hard not to be boring. Even with the circus surrounding City, Erling Haaland will almost certainly secure another Golden Boot.

Joao Pedro would be the one I might have backed to challenge him, but injury has stalled his challenge.

DS: Why would it be anyone other than Erling Haaland? It says a lot that even after the Norwegian was criticised in some circles for failing to score in City’s last two league games, the defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest, he is still sitting pretty on top of the leaderboard with nine goals in 10 league games.

The Golden Boot simply won’t be won by anyone else.

ST: It’s the boring answer but in a league lacking natural goalscsorers, Erling Haaland is the obvious pick. The Norwegian has been off the boil in recent weeks, but he always finds his way back into form.

No one knows where the back of the net is quite like Haaland. It’s that simple.

#1912. Liverpool injury news: Reds receive fresh Dominik Szoboszlai update ahead of Man United clash

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 00:33

Hungary boss Marco Rossi has insisted Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai is fit to play in Tuesday's UEFA Nations League clash against Northern Ireland.

Szoboszlai was forced off with a minor knee issue in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

As a result, there was some doubt as to whether he would link up with the Hungary squad for the final two matches of the Nations League league phase.

Not only did he join up with his national team, but he played the full duration of Saturday's 2-0 away win over Georgia, in which he provided an assist for Barnabas Varga's 85th-minute effort.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he was close to pulling out of the game after feeling the injury in the pre-match warm-up.

The midfielder also said his leg "felt good" during the game and that he would start the "treatment process all over again" in a bid to be ready for Tuesday's home meeting with Northern Ireland.

Speaking in Monday's pre-match press conference, Rossi attempted to ease fears over Szoboszlai's injury status, insisting his captain is ready to feature at the Puskas Arena.

“Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?” Rossi said.

“I didn’t see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

“I don’t think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don’t think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia.”

For Hungary, Tuesday's game is an important fixture as it offers the chance to secure promotion to League A of the Nations League.

Having collected 10 points from their five matches, Hungary enter the final matchday in second spot and one point behind leaders Northern Ireland in Group B2.

Meanwhile, Liverpool's main priority is Sunday's Premier League clash against Manchester United, who will start life under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will be keen to have Szoboszlai available for the home fixture, especially as there is doubt over Ryan Gravenberch's availability.

#1911. Pictured: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at airport before starting Manchester United role

Mauricio Pochettino has been pictured arriving in the UK for the first time as Manchester United manager.

The Argentine flew straight from the United States in the early hours of Wednesday morning and the Gulfstream G700 he was believed to be on was spotted landing at Manchester airport shortly before midday.

It was announced last week that the former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss was making a return to the Premier League, succeeding Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

However, the 54-year-old’s start to his fourth spell in English football was delayed as he finished up commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), overseeing an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals in his last game in charge.

Now after touching down in the UK, Pochettino can now take the next step in his career.

“I am ready [to return],” he told the Telegraph. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino is expected to head to Carrington immediately as he settles into his new role as Man United head coach, with the focus already shifting to his first game in charge against Liverpool on Sunday.

No goals have been scored either, which is obviously never ideal for a striker looking to grow. A loan move appears to be on the cards, but the January window isn’t for another month and a half, so a confidence boost cannot come quickly enough. Luckily, he got one last night.
